PullRequest.Title: explorer: Only auto-expand single children merged by compact folders
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #145510
Fixes #149084

Expanding a folder in the Explorer now only expands its single child when compact folders combines both into one row (like `a/b`), which that row needs to open in one click. Single child folders no longer expand on their own when compact folders is off, and a file nest that is a folder's only child now respects `explorer.fileNesting.expand`. Other trees using `autoExpandSingleChildren` (e.g. Call Stack) are unchanged.

**How to test**
1. With `"explorer.compactFolders": false`, expand a folder whose only child is a folder. The child stays collapsed, also after collapsing and expanding again and after Refresh Explorer.
2. With file nesting enabled and `"explorer.fileNesting.expand": false`, expand a folder whose only child is a file nest. The nest stays collapsed.
3. With compact folders on, click a combined row like `a/b`. It opens in one click.

Unit tests: `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/base/test/browser/ui/tree/*.test.js"` (88 passing)

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand a single-child directory chain in Explorer with compact folders enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expansion awaits ExplorerDataSource.getChildren; on a cold unresolved directory this awaits ExplorerItem.fetchChildren and fileService.resolve, then AsyncDataTree recursively materializes the already-resolved single-child descendants so the compressed row can reveal its children.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold resolve for the expanded directory; the service request includes the effective single-child descendant chain, and warm resolved nodes return cached children without another resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With autoExpandSingleChildren enabled, the same compact directory chain was recursively expanded after the same cold resolve.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cold resolve must complete before the compact chain is materialized and rendered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Depth of the compressible single-child directory chain; one boundary request serves the chain, while in-memory node creation/rendering scales linearly with chain depth.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The first unresolved directory performs one awaited resolve with resolveSingleChildDescendants; descendant traversal is recursive along the one-child chain, while any independently refreshable branches use Promises.settled. There is no new aggregate burst from the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold unresolved directories use one resolve that includes single-child descendants; _isDirectoryResolved makes subsequent descendant reads synchronous. Failures are not newly cached or retried by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicate returns true for exactly the compressible-directory case, and the data source's resolveSingleChildDescendants option establishes batching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem provider latency and practical chain depth vary, but boundary cardinality and recursion are unchanged from the prior compact-folder behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the new option preserves the prior work required for compressed folder rows and adds only constant-time compression/delegate checks per single-child node.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand or refresh a single-child folder with compact folders disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected folder's children are loaded, then the new predicate observes compression is disabled and stops automatic descendant materialization; rendering proceeds without recursively expanding the child.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected directory and request single-child descendants from the file service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold resolve for the selected folder, usually with descendant data batched by resolveSingleChildDescendants; zero additional resolves on warm model state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial resolve occurred, after which autoExpandSingleChildren recursively expanded and materialized every cached single child in the chain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected directory resolution remains on the expansion critical path, but automatic descendant tree processing is removed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Depth of a single-child folder chain; the diff removes linear descendant node refresh/render work when compression is disabled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most the selected folder's cold resolve is awaited. No descendant refresh promises are added by auto-expansion after the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold and warm filesystem behavior is unchanged; the Explorer model still batches and retains resolved child data. The tree now avoids consuming that prefetched chain solely for auto-expansion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tree.isCompressionEnabled() directly gates the new automatic expansion behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The saved CPU/rendering work depends on chain depth, but the direction is strictly reducing work.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improves or remains neutral; no reportable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand a folder whose only child is an incompressible file nest
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The folder children are loaded; ExplorerCompressionDelegate marks the file/nest node incompressible, so automatic expansion stops and the nest's synchronous nested children are not materialized unless separately expanded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the containing folder if it is cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold containing-folder resolve; nested file children are model-backed and synchronous.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: autoExpandSingleChildren automatically refreshed and rendered the sole nest child after loading the containing folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the containing-folder resolve blocks expansion; the diff removes automatic processing of the nest children.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of nested file children and frequency of folder refreshes; the diff avoids automatic nest-child processing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work or parallel boundary operation is introduced; nested children use ExplorerDataSource's synchronous fast path when requested.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Containing-folder resolution and nested-child model caching are unchanged; nested children are returned synchronously when explicitly requested.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ExplorerCompressionDelegate.isIncompressible is a constant-time property/type check and directly prevents the old automatic refresh.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File-nest sizes vary, but no added work exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the changed behavior removes eager tree work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use other AsyncDataTree or CompressibleAsyncDataTree consumers, including Call Stack
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setChildren performs the same singleton check and delegates to shouldAutoExpandSingleChild; consumers retaining autoExpandSingleChildren preserve the prior recursion, and consumers without either option stop after a constant-time false result.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of singleton child updates; each now includes one virtual method call, with no collection scan or allocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh scheduling and Promises.settled behavior are unchanged; no new task, IPC, filesystem, database, subprocess, or network operation is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key, miss handling, coalescing, or invalidation behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the base implementation returns the existing readonly boolean and preserves prior behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Invocation frequency varies by tree, but the added operation is constant-time and non-allocating.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression; the abstraction overhead is negligible and existing auto-expansion semantics remain unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced singleton expansion through AsyncDataTree recursion, compression state, ExplorerDataSource, ExplorerItem caching, and fileService.resolve. The PR preserves work for compressed directory chains and reduces recursive materialization elsewhere; no valid performance finding or evidenced shipped-regression record was identified.
